name: FAM voice bake-off passages
note: Three passages chosen to stress different things a FAM episode asks of a voice. Written in FAM's register per CLAUDE.md - speak from inside, every sentence carries information, land it and stop. Each is held to 40-50 words, inside the verified 25-59 word range of the real first-chunk corpus, so the test hears what the product would actually send. Numbers in passage 3 are SYNTHETIC, written to exercise number prosody; they are not market data and must never be quoted as such.

passages.label: intimate / curious storytelling
passages.stresses: warmth, small dynamic range, a turn that needs timing, a dry closing line that must not be over-sold
passages.watch_for: Does it sound like someone leaning in, or like an announcer? Does the joke in the last sentence land, or get flattened?
passages.text: The oldest lullaby anyone has found is four thousand years old, written in Babylonian, and it is not soothing. It warns the baby that it has woken the house god, and the god is angry. Parents have always bargained with exhaustion. They just used to write it down.

passages.label: energetic explanatory narration
passages.stresses: forward momentum, a colon and an em-dash, a three-verb run that needs rhythm, emphasis that must fall on the right word
passages.watch_for: Does 'move it' get the stress, or does the line go flat? Does the three-verb run accelerate, or plod? Is the last sentence emphatic without shouting?
passages.text: Here is what surprises people about heat pumps: they do not make heat. They move it. Even at freezing, outdoor air holds energy, and the pump squeezes it, concentrates it, and pushes it inside - four units of warmth for every one it uses. Nothing else does that.

passages.label: authoritative / news-style delivery
passages.stresses: proper nouns, decimals, a large number in words, percentages, a transition phrase, a colon mid-sentence
passages.watch_for: Are 'zero point four percent' and 'two point one percent' read naturally or spelled out awkwardly? Does 'Nasdaq' survive? Does 'Beneath that flatness' carry a genuine turn, or reset to a new sentence?
passages.text: Markets closed mixed on Thursday. The Nasdaq finished up zero point four percent, the Dow slipped one hundred and twelve points, and the S and P ended where it started. Beneath that flatness, semiconductors moved: Nvidia rose two point one percent, Intel fell three point eight.
